observation_summary: The compiler fails to display the last line of an error or warning message, particularly when the source file does not end with a newline character. This results in truncated error reports.
hypothesis: The logic responsible for extracting source lines for error reporting fails to handle the case where the requested line is the final line of the file and the file does not contain a trailing newline character. The code incorrectly assumes that if a newline character cannot be found, it should return null, even if there is still content remaining in the file buffer.
prediction: The fix will involve adding a check to verify if the current position has reached the end of the file, and if not, returning the remaining content of the file instead of returning null.
experiment_rationale: The provided diff shows that the code was updated to explicitly check if 'pos >= js.length()' and return the remaining substring if true, rather than unconditionally returning null. This confirms that the original logic was missing a boundary check for the end-of-file condition.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic 'Checking' defect. The original code lacked a necessary guard condition to handle the end-of-file boundary correctly when no newline character was present. The fix adds this missing check, ensuring that the final line of content is correctly returned instead of null.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the addition of an 'if (pos >= js.length())' check.
The bug report describes truncation of the last error/warning, which is consistent with failing to read the final line of a file.
The failing test 'testExceptNoNewLine' confirms that the system was returning null when it should have returned the final line of content.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic was updated, the root cause is specifically the missing validation of the boundary condition (end of file), which is the definition of a Checking defect.
